description: Astronova Cosmic Explorer is an interactive space mission platform built for NASA Space Apps. Designed for Artemis and Mars missions, it features an HD Solar System Explorer, a Star Catalog, and sixteen live browser tools—including light-delay, weight calculators, orbital velocity, mission elapsed time, and radiation estimators. Complete with ARIA, an offline AI assistant, it delivers zero-API-key mission planning and astrophysics insights directly in your browser.
summary: 🚀 Single-file  cosmic explorer for NASA Space Apps 2026. Solar system orbital view + 16 spaceflight calculators + 5 mini-game astronaut trainer + offline AI assistant (ARIA) + live NASA data widgets (APOD, Mars Rover photos, NASA Image Library, NeoWs asteroid tracker). Vanilla JS, no backend, no build step. Core runs offline; live NASA widgets activate with internet. Double-click index.html to run.
details:
Project Overview: AstroNova Cosmic Explorer

What it is: A single-file frontend web application built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.

Architecture: Combines HTML, CSS, and JavaScript inline. The core experience runs zero-backend and zero-install, with optional live NASA open-data integration through public REST APIs (APOD, Mars Rover Photos, NASA Image Library, and NeoWs). A free NASA DEMO_KEY (or registered key) is used for higher rate limits during live demos, but the app degrades gracefully to its offline knowledge base when offline.

1. What It Does & How It Works

  • Solar System Explorer: Interactive orbital view with the Sun at the center. Includes 9 planet orbits from Mercury through Pluto and the Moon attached to Earth. All bodies are clickable to open detailed HD datasheets.
  • Star Catalog: Catalog of notable stars. Each star includes magnitude ratings and physical statistics.
  • Space Mission Tools: 16 practical calculators that compute light-speed communication delays, weight on other worlds, orbital velocities, mission elapsed time, delta-v budgets, and radiation doses — all locally.
  • Live NASA Data Widgets: Real-time integration with four NASA open APIs — Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD), Mars Rover Photos (with keyless NASA Image Library fallback when the rover endpoint is unavailable), NASA Image & Video Library, and Near-Earth Object (NeoWs) tracking via CNEOS. All data is fetched client-side with graceful fallback when the network or API is unavailable.
  • Junior Astronaut Trainer: 5 progressive mission simulations. Each mission combines a 3D-themed mini-game with a 4-step decision-making briefing. Completing missions awards XP, badges, and a certification.
  • ARIA AI Chatbot: Built-in 100% offline knowledge engine using topic classification to answer space and project-related questions. No external LLM calls.

2. Project Benefits

  • Zero Friction: Core app runs instantly in any modern browser — opened locally or hosted on static platforms like GitHub Pages, Netlify, or Vercel. Live NASA widgets activate automatically when an internet connection is available.
  • Hybrid Architecture: Self-contained offline core (solar system, calculators, training missions, ARIA) plus live NASA data widgets. Operates fully offline with graceful degradation; requires no backend server or database.
  • Comprehensive Learning: Merges visual exploration, real spaceflight mathematics, gamified astronaut training, and live NASA mission data in a single lightweight package.

3. Intended Impact

  • Educational Engagement: Inspires students, youth, and space enthusiasts. Promotes learning about astronomy, celestial mechanics, and NASA's Artemis mission context.
  • Interactive Learning: Transforms complex spaceflight concepts into approachable experiences. Users learn through hands-on calculators, gamified mission challenges, and real NASA data exploration.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware, & Software

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript.
  • Software & Environment: Requires only a modern web browser. No external frameworks or libraries.
  • NASA Open Data APIs: api.nasa.gov/planetary/apod, api.nasa.gov/mars-photos/api/v1/rovers/, images-api.nasa.gov, api.nasa.gov/neo/rest/v1/ — called client-side via fetch().
  • Data & Graphics: Browser localStorage for cadet progress, HTML Canvas for the dynamic background starfield.

5. Project Creativity

  • Unified Experience: Seamlessly integrates an orbital solar system model, 16 advanced space mission calculators, an interactive cadet training program, and live NASA data widgets in one compact file.
  • Gamified Simulations: Custom browser-based mini-games simulating high-stakes space maneuvers such as Max-Q throttle management, docking alignment, and planetary entry sequences.
  • Built-in Offline AI: ARIA, a custom JavaScript keyword-matching and topic-classification engine, functions as an intelligent project guide without external LLM APIs.

6. Key Considerations by the Team

  • Accessibility: Prioritized ease of use by eliminating backend servers, installations, and build tools. The app works offline and on low-end hardware; NASA widgets require only a standard internet connection.
  • Scientific Accuracy: Grounded tools in authentic NASA reference physics and formulas, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, Hohmann transfers, and relativistic time dilation.
  • User Engagement: Progressive challenges, XP scoring, badges, and a formal graduation certificate reward learning and encourage completion.
